doc.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

chapter: Dance halls and learning jazz in Japan
title: Father's reaction to dance hall work
summary: Her father disapproved of a daughter playing in dance halls, but good pay and her mother's support won him over.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did your father feel about your continued involvement in music?

Well firstly he was very, very upset because in the Japanese, traditionally middle class family on, daughters are not supposed to work. They marry someone. And on top of that playing in dance halls, my God, that’s an evil place. But I was paid tremendous money in those days. And it was very helpful for the family. And coupled with that my mother sort

of talked him into it. Actually this was in the fall of ’46, and I was supposed to go to medical school. And the school in Japan starts in the springtime, so it’s not like September. So my mother said well until she starts school, so that cooled my father. Then by the time that came they thought well she didn’t become a juvenile delinquent or anything, so that was that.
Interesting. When did it first come up that you might actually come to the States to study?
